title: A solution (solution.yaml)
description: What a solution consists of: workflows (case types with their BPMN files), tables of rules (DMN files), texts, calculations, agents, measures, transcriptions and the settings the installation is asked for. Files are named relative to solution.yaml. Installing it again replaces its workflows and agents; what people changed in the installation (texts, tags, schedules, who decides, choices) stays as they left it.

decisions.description: The tables of rules (DMN files) it brings, among them the policy that judges its commands

instructions.description: Who the agent is and how it must decide

model.description: Which model it runs on; left out: the installation's

commands.description: Commands it may propose; it never carries them out itself

notesGaps.description: true: it notes what it could not find in the knowledge, for a person to fill in

helpers.description: Other agents it may ask for help, with what each is asked for

checker.description: The agent that checks each decision

attempts.description: How many times it may decide when the checker asks for changes

spendLimit.description: Dollars one decision may cost at most, helpers and checks included

claims.description: Values it gives with the words they rest on: true for any, or which values and what happens when the words are not found (mark them, or a person checks)

corrections.description: How many times an answer that cannot be used is sent back to it (0 to 3)

replans.description: How many times it decides again when an action it proposed did not go through (0 to 3)

senior.description: The agent asked to settle what it cannot

waitMinutes.description: A system not answering or data missing: wait this long, then ask again

permits.description: Whether a person may allow it once what it may not propose

permitted.description: With selected: what may be allowed once

situationLimit.description: Dollars settling one unusual situation may cost at most

whenStuck.description: What it does when it cannot settle a case as asked

process.description: Its BPMN file (workflow.json says what it may contain)

processKey.description: The id of the process in that file

startOn.description: The types of event that open a case of it

startWhen.description: An expression an event must also meet, such as ${event.status == 'PAID'}

policy.description: The table of rules that judges its commands: which go out, which wait for a person, which are refused

shadow.description: true: Test run. It records the actions it would take and sends none. A new workflow starts so.

tags.description: What people find the workflow by

on.description: For a week the days' names; for a month 1 to 31 or last

schedule.description: Times it opens a case by itself, in the installation's time zone

takesFrom.description: The channel connections it takes messages from; ["*"] for every channel

options.description: Ways it may do some of its work; read in the workflow as ${options.<key>}

measures.description: The solution's measures its cases keep, each with the expression its value comes from

creditLater.description: Its cases take money that comes in after they closed

stillUseful.description: Until when a stopped case of it is still worth carrying on

named.description: With named: a value of the case that names the person, such as {{connector.crm.record.fields.owner}}

role.description: With role: a role of People

fallbackRole.description: May decide too after afterHours working hours, when the person is away or unknown

whoDecides.description: Who decides its actions that wait for approval; anybody who may approve when not said

tenantId.description: This entry is one tenant's own version of the workflow

file.description: The text, with places for values in double braces: {{connector.<connection>.<thing>.<detail>}}, {{settings.<key>}}, {{#name}}...{{/name}} kept only when there is such a value, {{> key}} another text
A calculation written line by line (calculation.schema.json), or the business's own Excel model (.xlsx)

kind.description: money with a currency; steps with steps, earns and ends; time worked out from a steps measure (of, from, to)

earnedWhen.description: For money: the steps measure whose earning step makes it earned

key.description: Read in workflows and texts as settings.<key>
